szwarcberg-2026-register-jumps.note: the authors' arXiv version (v3): a register hole opened on a sounding first register reaches the second over a narrower range of blowing pressure than the second's whole stability, its success in places depending on the phase it is opened at, transients up to seconds long where quasi-periodic regimes lie between; the upward twelfth, on an artificial player and a model, no players timed

campidell-widholm-1995-valve-slurs.title: The influence of valve mechanism of brass wind instruments on the microstructure of slurs - new results
campidell-widholm-1995-valve-slurs.in: Speech - Music - Hearing, Proceedings of the 32nd Czech Conference on Acoustics, Prague, 87-90
campidell-widholm-1995-valve-slurs.noDoi: the 32nd Czech Conference on Acoustics' proceedings have none (Crossref, 15 November 2026: only Widholm's paper of nearly the same title at ISMA 1997, doi:10.25144/15170, another paper)
campidell-widholm-1995-valve-slurs.note: a trumpet's input impedance measured at 30 steps of a valve's travel, and the slurs a musician played across it (g5-Bb5 and others; Perinet and rotary valves): where the half-pressed valve leaves a wide impedance 'valley' between the two notes' peaks, the standing wave breaks down, 'for a short time the tone sounds weak', a 'noise band' often heard, the played frequency's trace broken for some 0.1 s (fig. 3); where the impedance stays high, a continuous slur. The valley's shape set by the valve's place along the tube (a half-pressed valve reflects as the tube's end there), its width by the valve's bore; a well-trained player bridges a valley quickly. No DOI

logie-chick-stevenson-campbell-2010-slur.authors: S. Logie, J. P. Chick, S. Stevenson, M. Campbell
logie-chick-stevenson-campbell-2010-slur.title: Upward and downward slurred transients on brass instruments: why is one not simply the inverse of the other?
logie-chick-stevenson-campbell-2010-slur.noDoi: the 10e Congres Francais d'Acoustique's papers have none: HAL holds it, hal-00539675 (Crossref, 15 November 2026: none)
logie-chick-stevenson-campbell-2010-slur.note: two horn players' octave lip slurs (D3-D4, 4th to 8th modes and 3rd to 6th) by high-speed camera and microphones: one player's upward slur has 'the radiated sound almost inaudible for a period of 20-25 ms before the note D4 begins to sound'; the other sounds the modes between, each some 10 ms, some 50 cents below them; downward slurs pass through the intermediate modes too. Brass starting transients some 50 ms (Luce & Clark 1967). No DOI

hruska-svejda-gustar-2015-trumpet-transi.authors: V. Hruska, M. Svejda, M. Gustar
hruska-svejda-gustar-2015-trumpet-transi.title: Transients of trumpet tone: basic links between perception and measurements of lips opening surface and pressure in player's mouth
hruska-svejda-gustar-2015-trumpet-transi.in: Proceedings of the Third Vienna Talk on Music Acoustics, Vienna, urn:nbn:at:at-ubmw-20151022110955643-1586116-8
hruska-svejda-gustar-2015-trumpet-transi.noDoi: the Vienna Talk's proceedings have none: its URN is urn:nbn:at:at-ubmw-20151022110955643-1586116-8 (Crossref, 15 November 2026: none)
hruska-svejda-gustar-2015-trumpet-transi.note: one semi-professional trumpeter (pilot study) by high-speed imaging and mouth pressure: a slow lip slur F4-Bb4 at mf, the lips not fully closing for 0.2-0.25 s, the upper harmonics fading before the mode changes; the slur downward less demanding, a looser player's showing an audible attack at it. No valve slurs. No DOI

harran-1973-vicentino.title: Vicentino and His Rules of Text Underlay
harran-1973-vicentino.note: Vicentino's twelve rules (L'antica musica ridotta alla moderna prattica, 1555), four of them Lanfranco's (Scintille di musica, 1533): two vowels across a rest of a minim or a semibreve are not elided, "for there one retains the procedure of speech, having as an ending that stop" (his rule 9) -- a rest an ending: registry/method/underlay.json midWord

harran-1978-origins.title: In Pursuit of Origins: The Earliest Writing on Text Underlay (c. 1440)
harran-1978-origins.note: the Venetian folio (Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana, Lat. 336, c. 1440) in facsimile, transcription and translation; not read here, known through drake-2006 (research/SOURCES_TO_FETCH.md)

king-1999.title: Texting Practices in Manuscript Sources of Early Fifteenth-Century Polyphony
king-1999.in: Journal of the Royal Musical Association 124(1), 1-25
king-1999.note: the Venetian folio of c. 1440 transcribed and translated (pp. 3-4): "there is no rule according to which one must adapt words to a melody other than the understanding of whoever has to place them"; its examples let a rest fall within a word. Not read here, known through drake-2006 (research/SOURCES_TO_FETCH.md)

drake-2006.title: The contemporary perception of text-music relations in motets c.1500
drake-2006.noDoi: a doctoral thesis without one (University of Glasgow): theses.gla.ac.uk/5644, its redacted PDF
drake-2006.note: composers c. 1500 "were not operating with an unwritten theory about word-tone relations"; the Venetian folio of c. 1440 in King's translation, its examples letting a rest fall within a word -- "Chi-ri-e" among them -- while a repeated note takes a new syllable (pp. 23-25): registry/method/underlay.json midWord
